findings.evidence: template/scripts/github_read_cache.py `_store` loads the entire file, sets one key and rewrites everything (lines 316-331). Nothing removes entries for closed or merged PRs, old comment-history URLs or old issue numbers. The file grows with every distinct URL ever read. Each later page write costs O(file size), and each `_page` call re-parses the whole file via `_load` (line 370). On a busy coordinator with parallel overview threads this adds contention and slowness over time.
findings.summary: The cache never evicts entries, and every 200 response rewrites the whole file under a global lock.

findings.evidence:
template/scripts/github_read_cache.py:336-338 first does `stdout.partition("

")`. With CRLF headers (`

`) it only falls back to normalised splitting if no '

' exists anywhere in the output. If the body contains '

' (for example pretty-printed JSON), the header/body boundary is misplaced. The result is a misparsed Link/ETag or a JSON decode error. Normalising CRLF first would be safer.
findings.summary: `parse_response` splits headers from body on the first '\n\n' before it normalises CRLF, so a CRLF response whose body contains a blank line is split in the wrong place.
